author: Hakim Abul-Qasim Ferdowsi Tusi (new, lesser-known quote)
persian: چو گفتار نیکو بود، گوش دار / که نیکو سخن خود بود یادگار
english_translation: When speech is good, listen carefully / For good words are themselves a lasting memorial.
theme: Worthy speech deserves attentive ears and becomes its own living monument

author: Hakim Abul-Qasim Ferdowsi Tusi (new, lesser-known quote)
persian: نگر تا نگردی تو ایمن ز دشمن / که دشمن چو آتش بود در نشیمن
english_translation: Take care that you never feel safe from an enemy / For an enemy is like fire in your dwelling.
theme: Perpetual vigilance against adversity as a fundamental requirement of survival

author: Abu Nasr al-Farabi (Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Farabi)
persian: شهر فاضله آن است که در آن انسان به سعادت حقیقی برسد
english_translation: The virtuous city is the one in which human beings attain true happiness.
theme: The ideal society measured solely by its capacity to foster genuine human flourishing

author: Abu Nasr al-Farabi (Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Farabi)
persian: رئیس اول آن است که نه فرمان‌برد نه کسی بر او برتری جوید
english_translation: The first ruler is one who obeys no one and over whom no one seeks supremacy.
theme: The philosopher-king as the ideal ruler — self-sufficient in wisdom and answerable to none

author: Abu Nasr al-Farabi (Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Farabi)
persian: موسیقی روح را آن می‌کند که ورزش جسم را
english_translation: Music does for the soul what exercise does for the body.
theme: Music as the essential nourishment and exercise of the human soul

author: Abu Nasr al-Farabi (Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Farabi)
persian: غایت فلسفه شناخت موجودات است آن‌چنان که هستند
english_translation: The purpose of philosophy is to know existing things as they truly are.
theme: Philosophy's highest purpose as the unflinching perception of reality as it truly is

author: Ikhwan al-Safa (Brethren of Purity, Persian encyclopedists)
persian: فلسفه آن است که آدمی تا آنجا که توانایی دارد شبیه به خدا شود
english_translation: Philosophy is for a person to become, insofar as they are able, similar to God.
theme: The telos of philosophy as the gradual divinization of the human being

author: Ikhwan al-Safa (Brethren of Purity, Persian encyclopedists)
persian: علوم سه‌گانه‌اند: علم بدن، علم نفس، علم الهی / و کمال آدمی در جمع هر سه
english_translation: The sciences are threefold: knowledge of the body, knowledge of the soul, and knowledge of the divine / Human perfection lies in combining all three.
theme: Complete human development requires integrating bodily, psychological, and spiritual knowledge

author: Zakariya al-Razi (Muhammad ibn Zakariya al-Razi / Rhazes)
persian: عقل بزرگ‌ترین نعمت خداست / پس از آن فروگذار مکن
english_translation: Reason is God's greatest gift / So do not abandon it.
theme: Reason as the supreme divine gift that carries the moral obligation never to be abandoned

author: Zakariya al-Razi (Muhammad ibn Zakariya al-Razi / Rhazes)
persian: پزشک که بیمار خود را نشناسد، درمان او نتواند
english_translation: A physician who does not know their patient cannot heal them.
theme: True healing requires knowing the whole person, not merely treating the disease

author: Zakariya al-Razi (Muhammad ibn Zakariya al-Razi / Rhazes)
persian: فیلسوف آن است که دانش را برای دانش دوست بدارد، نه برای سود
english_translation: A philosopher is one who loves knowledge for knowledge's sake, not for gain.
theme: Pure love of knowledge as the defining quality of the true philosopher

author: Abu Rayhan al-Biruni (new, additional quote)
persian: مسافر باید چشم باز داشته باشد / که جهان هر جا درسی می‌دهد
english_translation: The traveler must keep eyes open / For the world offers a lesson everywhere.
theme: Travel with open eyes as one of the most reliable schools of wisdom

author: Abu Rayhan al-Biruni (new, additional quote)
persian: تعصب آفت علم است / که هر که تعصب دارد، راه دانش را بسته است
english_translation: Prejudice is the plague of knowledge / For whoever holds prejudice has closed the road to learning.
theme: Prejudice as the most deadly enemy of genuine knowledge and open inquiry

author: Khwandamir (Ghiyath al-Din ibn Humam al-Din Muhammad)
persian: آن که تاریخ را نخواند، محکوم به تکرار آن است
english_translation: One who does not read history is condemned to repeat it.
theme: Historical knowledge as the only shield against the repetition of past catastrophes

author: Khwandamir (Ghiyath al-Din ibn Humam al-Din Muhammad)
persian: شاهان را اگر عدل باشد، ملک پاید / وگر ظلم باشد، ملک نپاید
english_translation: If kings have justice, their kingdom endures / If they have oppression, their kingdom does not endure.
theme: Justice as the cornerstone upon which all enduring power is built

author: Vasifi (Zayn al-Din Mahmud Vasifi)
persian: عمر آدمی دو روز است / یک روز به کسب ادب و یک روز به کار بستن آن
english_translation: A person's life consists of two days / One day for acquiring culture and one day for putting it to work.
theme: Life's ideal division between the acquisition of wisdom and its active application

author: Jalaluddin Davani (new, different quote)
persian: انسان کامل آینه‌ی تمام‌نمای وجود است
english_translation: The perfect human being is the full-reflecting mirror of existence.
theme: The fully realized human being as the supreme mirror in which all of existence sees itself

author: Lutfi of Samarkand (Mawlana Lutfi)
persian: عشق آن است که در آن خود را فراموش کنی / نه آن که خود را به یاد آوری
english_translation: Love is that in which you forget yourself / Not that which brings you to remember yourself.
theme: Genuine love defined by the complete forgetting of the self, not its enhancement

author: Hilali Jagatai (Badr al-Din Hilali)
persian: آن که در عشق شکیبا است، عاشق راستین است / که عشق آزمایشی است و صبر پاسخ آن
english_translation: One who is patient in love is the true lover / For love is a test and patience is its answer.
theme: Patience as the only worthy response to love's inevitable tests and trials

author: Mushtaq Ali Shah (Persian Sufi tradition)
persian: آن که از دنیا گذشت، به حق رسید / آن که در دنیا ماند، در خود ماند
english_translation: One who passed beyond the world arrived at the divine / One who remained in the world remained within themselves.
theme: Transcendence of worldly attachment as the path from the self to the divine

author: Hazin Lahiji (Muhammad Ali Hazin Lahiji)
persian: عارف را بهشت و دوزخ یکی است / که عارف فراتر از هر دو است
english_translation: For the mystic, paradise and hell are one / For the mystic has transcended both.
theme: The true mystic transcending the duality of heaven and hell to reach undivided reality

author: Hazin Lahiji (Muhammad Ali Hazin Lahiji)
persian: غم غربت آن است که نه جا داری و نه یار / که در غربت، یار جای را می‌پوشاند
english_translation: The sorrow of exile is having neither home nor companion / For in exile, a companion covers for the lack of home.
theme: Companionship as the one thing that can make exile bearable by serving as home

author: Shah Ni'matullah Wali (Nur ud-Din Shah Ni'matullah ibn Abdullah Kirmani)
persian: دلم دریاست و عشق موج آن / کجا مرا آرام و قرار؟
english_translation: My heart is a sea and love is its wave / Where shall I find rest and stillness?
theme: The heart consumed by love as a sea that can never be completely stilled

author: Shah Ni'matullah Wali (Nur ud-Din Shah Ni'matullah ibn Abdullah Kirmani)
persian: آنچه هستی آنی / و آنچه نیستی آنی نیستی
english_translation: What you are, that you are / And what you are not, that you are not.
theme: The radical simplicity of authentic self-knowledge — you are exactly what you are, no more

author: Qadir Khan Khattak (Khushal Khan Khattak, Persian literary tradition)
persian: مرد آن است که در میدان نماند، بلکه میدان را تغییر دهد
english_translation: A true man is not one who merely holds the field, but one who changes it.
theme: True heroism not in passive endurance but in actively transforming the field of struggle

author: Hakim Shafa'i Isfahani
persian: آن که دانا بود و خاموش نشست / از آن که نادان بود و پرگو، برتر است
english_translation: One who is wise and sits in silence / Is superior to one who is ignorant and talkative.
theme: Silent wisdom surpassing loud ignorance as the measure of true intellectual worth

author: Waqif Lahori
persian: عمر گذشت و ما هنوز در آغازیم / که سفر دانش را پایانی نیست
english_translation: Life passed and we are still at the beginning / For the journey of knowledge has no end.
theme: A life of learning revealing, at its close, that one has only reached the beginning

author: Mirza Talib Amuli
persian: از تجربه چیزی آموختم که از کتاب نیاموختم
english_translation: From experience I learned what I could not learn from books.
theme: Lived experience as a teacher that surpasses all that can be learned from written texts

author: Mirza Talib Amuli
persian: آن که می‌گوید ولی نمی‌کند، چراغی است که خود را می‌سوزاند
english_translation: One who speaks but does not act is a lamp that burns itself.
theme: Empty words without corresponding action consuming their speaker like a self-immolating flame

author: Mushfiq Kashifi (Khwaja Kamil ud-Din Kashifi)
persian: ادب تاج سر است / که هر که ادب داشت، سربلند بود
english_translation: Courtesy is the crown of the head / Whoever has courtesy walks with head held high.
theme: Refined manners and courtesy as the most visible crown of genuine character

author: Maktabi Shirazi
persian: عشق را زبان نیست، اما همه می‌فهمند
english_translation: Love has no tongue, yet everyone understands it.
theme: Love as a wordless universal language understood across all boundaries of speech

author: Fighani Shirazi (Baba Fighani)
persian: در دل شکسته گنجینه‌ای است / که در دل درست نتوان یافت
english_translation: In a broken heart there is a treasure / That cannot be found in an unbroken one.
theme: The broken heart as the sacred vessel that holds what the whole, untroubled heart never can

author: Fighani Shirazi (Baba Fighani)
persian: سوختن شمع آن نیست که خاموش شود / بلکه آن است که تا آخر بسوزد
english_translation: The burning of a candle is not that it goes out / But that it burns to the very end.
theme: A life well lived is one that burns completely and to the end, not one that simply avoids going out

author: Ahli Shirazi (Muhammad ibn Yusuf Ahli Shirazi)
persian: عشق پیر نمی‌شود / که آتش جوان می‌ماند تا بسوزد
english_translation: Love does not grow old / For fire remains young as long as it burns.
theme: Love as an eternal fire that remains forever young as long as its flame endures

author: Ahli Shirazi (Muhammad ibn Yusuf Ahli Shirazi)
persian: کسی که خود را نشناخت، دیگران را نخواهد شناخت
english_translation: One who has not known themselves will not know others.
theme: Self-knowledge as the foundational prerequisite for all genuine knowledge of others

author: Naziri Nishapuri (Muhammad Husayn Naziri Nishapuri)
persian: دریای محبت را ساحل نیست / هر که فرو رفت، راه برگشت نیست
english_translation: The ocean of love has no shore / Whoever sinks in it has no way back.
theme: True love as a boundless ocean from which there is no return for those who truly enter it

author: Naziri Nishapuri (Muhammad Husayn Naziri Nishapuri)
persian: سخن آینه‌ی دل است / هر چه در دل باشد، در سخن پیداست
english_translation: Speech is the mirror of the heart / Whatever is in the heart is visible in speech.
theme: Every utterance as an involuntary revelation of the heart's true contents

author: Talib Amuli (Mir Muhammad Talib Amuli)
persian: هنرمند کسی است که از ناچیز، ارزش بسازد
english_translation: An artist is one who creates value from the insignificant.
theme: Artistic genius as the capacity to transmute the ordinary and overlooked into something of value

author: Sa'ib Tabrizi (Muhammad Ali Sa'ib Tabrizi)
persian: خاری که امروز از پا بکشی / دردی است که فردا نخواهی کشید
english_translation: A thorn you remove from your foot today / Is a pain you will not endure tomorrow.
theme: Dealing with small problems promptly as the surest way to prevent large suffering later

author: Sa'ib Tabrizi (Muhammad Ali Sa'ib Tabrizi)
persian: عیب خود دیدن هنر است / که هر که عیب خود دید، راه اصلاح یافت
english_translation: Seeing one's own faults is an art / For whoever sees their own faults has found the path to correction.
theme: The rare art of seeing one's own faults clearly as the necessary first step toward correction

author: Sa'ib Tabrizi (Muhammad Ali Sa'ib Tabrizi)
persian: از خار تجربه، گل معرفت می‌روید
english_translation: From the thorns of experience, the flower of wisdom grows.
theme: Painful experience as the thorny soil from which genuine wisdom ultimately flowers

author: Sa'ib Tabrizi (Muhammad Ali Sa'ib Tabrizi)
persian: آیینه‌ای باش که عیب نشان دهد / نه دیواری که عیب را پنهان کند
english_translation: Be a mirror that reveals flaws / Not a wall that conceals them.
theme: Honest, mirror-like friendship that reveals truth as infinitely more valuable than flattering concealment

author: Kalim Kashani (Abu Talib Kalim Kashani)
persian: شکستن دل آسان است / ساختن دل سخت‌ترین کار دنیاست
english_translation: Breaking a heart is easy / Mending a heart is the hardest work in the world.
theme: The ease of destruction versus the immense difficulty of healing and restoration

author: Kalim Kashani (Abu Talib Kalim Kashani)
persian: هر که گوشه‌ی عزلت گرفت، با جهانی نشست
english_translation: Whoever took a corner of solitude sat with the whole world.
theme: The paradox that true solitude opens into the fullest possible encounter with the whole world

author: Zuhuri Tursheizi (Nur al-Din Muhammad Zuhuri Tursheizi)
persian: قلم فکر را به دام می‌اندازد / که فکر بی‌قلم چون پرنده‌ی بی‌لانه است
english_translation: The pen captures thought in its net / For thought without a pen is like a bird without a nest.
theme: Writing as the nest that gives thought a fixed dwelling before it flies away forever

author: Zuhuri Tursheizi (Nur al-Din Muhammad Zuhuri Tursheizi)
persian: از تنهایی نهراس / که تنها آن است که با خود تنهاست
english_translation: Do not fear solitude / For truly alone is one who is alone with themselves — and cannot bear it.
theme: True loneliness is inner emptiness — those who can dwell with themselves are never truly alone

author: Fayz Kashani (Muhammad ibn Shah Murtada al-Kashani)
persian: دل به قدر ظرفیت خود می‌گیرد / هر که ظرفش بزرگ‌تر، بیشتر می‌یابد
english_translation: The heart receives according to its own capacity / Whoever has the larger vessel finds more.
theme: Spiritual receptivity proportional to the breadth and purity of the heart

author: Fayz Kashani (Muhammad ibn Shah Murtada al-Kashani)
persian: عالم آخرت مزرعه‌ی اعمال دنیاست
english_translation: The hereafter is the harvest field of the deeds of this world.
theme: The hereafter as the inevitable harvest of every seed of action planted in this life

author: Mir Najat Isfahani
persian: بی‌نیازی از مردم، بزرگ‌ترین ثروت است
english_translation: Independence from people's approval is the greatest wealth.
theme: Freedom from dependence on others' approval as the highest and most liberating form of wealth

author: Mir Najat Isfahani
persian: آرامش آن نیست که آشوبی نباشد / بلکه آن است که در آشوب آرام باشی
english_translation: Peace is not the absence of turmoil / But the ability to remain calm within turmoil.
theme: True inner peace as equanimity maintained in the very midst of chaos and upheaval

author: Mir Najat Isfahani
persian: هر که درد ندید، شادی را نشناخت / که شادی در سایه‌ی درد پرورش می‌یابد
english_translation: Whoever has not seen pain has not known joy / For joy is nurtured in the shadow of pain.
theme: Joy fully known only by those who have first endured the depth of pain

author: Ghanimat Kunjahi
persian: نغمه‌ی دل را کسی می‌شنود / که خود دلی داشته باشد
english_translation: The melody of the heart is heard only by one / Who themselves possesses a heart.
theme: Only those who have cultivated genuine feeling can perceive and receive the feelings of others

author: Arzu Khurasani
persian: آن که سخن بسیار گوید، کم می‌اندیشد / آن که کم گوید، بسیار می‌اندیشد
english_translation: One who speaks much thinks little / One who speaks little thinks much.
theme: The inverse relationship between the volume of speech and the depth of thought

author: Hatim Tai (Arab-Persian legendary figure of generosity)
persian: آنچه دادم را دارم / آنچه خوردم رفت / آنچه اندوختم نه از من ماند نه از دیگران
english_translation: What I gave, I still possess / What I ate is gone / What I hoarded remained for neither me nor others.
theme: The paradox of giving: only what is given away is truly and permanently possessed

author: Rumi (entirely new quote, not in prior sets)
persian: نه شرقی‌ام نه غربی / من نه از زمینم نه از آسمان / نه از آب و خاکم نه از بادم
english_translation: I am neither Eastern nor Western / I am neither of the earth nor of the heavens / I am neither of water and earth, nor of wind.
theme: The mystic's identity as universal — beyond all geographic, elemental, and temporal categories

author: Rumi (entirely new quote, not in prior sets)
persian: جان که فارغ شد از عشق، مُرد / زندگانی عاشقی را بُرد
english_translation: The soul that became free of love, died / It is love that sustains all life.
theme: Love as the animating principle of existence — without it the soul is merely dead

author: Rumi (entirely new quote, not in prior sets)
persian: تن آدمی شریف است به جان آدمی / نه به جامه‌ی زری و ابریشمی
english_translation: The human body is ennobled by the human soul / Not by garments of gold thread and silk.
theme: Human dignity rooted solely in the soul's quality, not in external wealth or adornment

author: Hafez (entirely new quote, not in prior sets)
persian: مرا روزی است با آن ماه روی / که هم شب باشد آن روز و هم روی
english_translation: I have a day with that moon-faced beloved / Where that day is both night and bright day.
theme: Love's union as a state beyond ordinary time where day and night are dissolved into one

author: Hafez (entirely new quote, not in prior sets)
persian: عیب رندان مکن ای زاهد پاکیزه سرشت / که گناه دگران بر تو نخواهند نوشت
english_translation: Do not blame the pleasure-seekers, O pure-natured ascetic / For the sins of others will not be written against your account.
theme: Each person accountable only for their own deeds — judging others serves no moral purpose

author: Hafez (entirely new quote, not in prior sets)
persian: عشق آتش است و من پروانه‌وار / می‌سوزم و می‌چرخم بر گِرد یار
english_translation: Love is fire and I, like a moth / Burn and circle around my beloved.
theme: The lover's willing self-immolation in the fire of love, like a moth circling a flame

author: Saadi Shirazi (entirely new quote, not in prior sets)
persian: هر که پند نپذیرد، آزموده باید که بیند / آزموده را آزمودن خطاست
english_translation: Whoever does not accept counsel must learn through experience / But to repeat what has already been experienced is an error.
theme: The highest error is to repeat what experience has already taught — counsel exists to spare us this

author: Saadi Shirazi (entirely new quote, not in prior sets)
persian: خدا را بر آن بنده بخشایش است / که خلق از وجودش در آسایش است
english_translation: God's mercy is upon the servant / Whose existence brings ease to others.
theme: Divine grace flowing most abundantly to those whose presence brings peace and relief to others

author: Saadi Shirazi (entirely new quote, not in prior sets)
persian: هنر چشمه است و جهل بیابان / هنرمند سیراب است و نادان تشنه
english_translation: Skill is a spring and ignorance a desert / The skilled one is sated and the ignorant one thirsts.
theme: Cultivated skill as an inexhaustible spring against the barren thirst of ignorance

author: Omar Khayyam (entirely new quote, not in prior sets)
persian: ما لعبتگانیم و فلک لعبت‌باز / از روی حقیقتی نه از روی مجاز
english_translation: We are the puppets and the sky is the puppet-master / This is a reality, not a metaphor.
theme: The sober philosophical recognition that human free will may be largely an illusion of cosmic fate

author: Omar Khayyam (entirely new quote, not in prior sets)
persian: من می‌خورم و هر که چو من اهل بود / می خوردن من به نزد او سهل بود
english_translation: I drink wine, and whoever is like me in knowledge / Will find my wine-drinking an easy matter.
theme: Tolerance as the natural fruit of genuine understanding and philosophical depth

author: Attar of Nishapur (entirely new quote, not in prior sets)
persian: مرغ دلم در قفس تن محبوس است / کی آزاد شوم؟ وقتی که تن را فراموش کنم
english_translation: The bird of my heart is imprisoned in the cage of the body / When will I be free? When I forget the body.
theme: Liberation of the soul achieved through transcendence and forgetting of bodily identity

author: Attar of Nishapur (entirely new quote, not in prior sets)
persian: آن که طالب حقیقت است، اول باید کاذب را بشناسد
english_translation: One who seeks truth must first learn to recognize falsehood.
theme: Discernment of falsehood as the necessary first step on any genuine path toward truth

author: Nizami Ganjavi (entirely new quote, not in prior sets)
persian: دل سلطان است و تن کشور او / آن که دل را گرفت، کشور را گرفت
english_translation: The heart is the sultan and the body its kingdom / Whoever captures the heart captures the kingdom.
theme: The heart as the true seat of sovereign power — conquer it and all else follows

author: Nizami Ganjavi (entirely new quote, not in prior sets)
persian: قصه‌گو حکیم است اگر قصه درست باشد / که داستان آیینه‌ی روزگار است
english_translation: The storyteller is a sage if the story is true / For the tale is the mirror of the age.
theme: True storytelling as a form of wisdom that holds up a mirror to the truth of its era

author: Fakhruddin Gurgani (new, different quote)
persian: آن که در درد است، دل را می‌شناسد / آن که در راحتی است، از دل بی‌خبر است
english_translation: One who is in pain knows the heart / One who is in comfort is ignorant of the heart.
theme: Suffering as the tutor that teaches genuine knowledge of the human heart

author: Sanai Ghaznavi (entirely new quote, not in prior sets)
persian: نفس خود را بشناس پیش از آنکه دیگری تو را بشناساند
english_translation: Know your own ego before another reveals it to you.
theme: Proactive self-knowledge as protection against the humiliation of having one's flaws exposed by others

author: Sanai Ghaznavi (entirely new quote, not in prior sets)
persian: هر که آموخت و عمل نکرد / دانشش زنگ زد و ضایع شد
english_translation: Whoever learned but did not act / Their knowledge rusted and went to waste.
theme: Knowledge left unapplied rusts and deteriorates like an unused tool left to the weather

author: Jami (entirely new quote, not in prior sets)
persian: عالم هستی آینه‌ی حق است / هر که را چشم باز باشد، حق را بیند
english_translation: The world of existence is the mirror of the divine / Whoever has open eyes sees the divine in it.
theme: The entire world as a vast mirror of the divine for those with the clarity of vision to see it

author: Jami (entirely new quote, not in prior sets)
persian: دانا بر نادان رحم آورد / که نادان ره گم کرده است و خود نمی‌داند
english_translation: The wise shows compassion to the ignorant / For the ignorant has lost the way and does not know it.
theme: The truly wise respond to ignorance not with contempt but with compassion for the lost

author: Abu Said Abil Kheir (entirely new quote, not in prior sets)
persian: هر که در کوی عشق قدم نهاد / از خود بیرون آمد و به حق رسید
english_translation: Whoever set foot in the lane of love / Stepped out of themselves and arrived at the divine.
theme: Love as the precise pathway out of the imprisoning self and into the freedom of the divine

author: Abu Said Abil Kheir (entirely new quote, not in prior sets)
persian: تصوف آن است که آنچه داری بدهی / و آنچه نداری بیابی
english_translation: Sufism is to give away what you have / And to find what you do not have.
theme: Sufi poverty as a paradox: emptying oneself of what is possessed to gain what cannot be possessed

author: Ruzbihan Baqli (Ruzbihan ibn Abi Nasr Baqli Shirazi)
persian: زیبایی تجلی حق است و دیدار آن عبادت
english_translation: Beauty is the manifestation of the divine, and beholding it is worship.
theme: The contemplation of beauty as a legitimate and genuine form of spiritual worship

author: Ruzbihan Baqli (Ruzbihan ibn Abi Nasr Baqli Shirazi)
persian: عارف در هر صورتی جمال حق را می‌بیند
english_translation: The mystic sees the beauty of the divine in every form.
theme: Mystical vision that perceives the divine beauty shining through every created form

author: Ruzbihan Baqli (Ruzbihan ibn Abi Nasr Baqli Shirazi)
persian: عشق حقیقی آن است که نه از ترس باشد نه از طمع / بلکه از سرشت ذات
english_translation: True love is that which comes neither from fear nor from greed / But from the very nature of being.
theme: Authentic love arising purely from the innermost nature of being — untainted by fear or desire

author: Mahmud Shabestari (new, different quote from Part 3)
persian: هر که بیرون جست از خود را / یافت در هر ذره معشوق خود را
english_translation: Whoever sought outside themselves / Found their beloved in every particle.
theme: Stepping outside the self reveals the beloved's presence in every particle of existence

author: Allama Iqbal (new, different quote from Part 3)
persian: در سینه‌ی کوه آتشفشانی است / در سینه‌ی مرد همتی والاست
english_translation: Within the mountain lies a volcano / Within the person of high resolve lies a noble aspiration.
theme: The dormant volcanic power within every person of genuine aspiration and resolve

author: Allama Iqbal (new, different quote from Part 3)
persian: از خاک برخیز و آسمانی شو / که خاک تو را نگه نمی‌دارد
english_translation: Rise from the earth and become heavenly / For the earth cannot hold you.
theme: The divine summons to transcend earthly limitations and rise to one's heavenly potential

author: Persian Proverb (unique, not in prior sets)
persian: هر که گندم کارد، گندم درود / هر که جو کارد، جو درود
english_translation: Whoever plants wheat, harvests wheat / Whoever plants barley, harvests barley.
theme: The exact and reliable correspondence between what one plants in life and what one harvests

author: Persian Proverb (unique, not in prior sets)
persian: آتش که نداری، دود هم نداری
english_translation: If you have no fire, you have no smoke either.
theme: Every visible effect proves an invisible cause — where there is no fire, no smoke can exist

author: Persian Proverb (unique, not in prior sets)
persian: آنقدر بزن که پنبه دنده شود
english_translation: Strike until the cotton becomes thread.
theme: Sustained, patient effort as the force that transforms raw potential into refined product

author: Persian Proverb (unique, not in prior sets)
persian: آش نخورده دهان سوخته
english_translation: The mouth burned from soup not yet eaten.
theme: The futility of suffering in anticipation of a harm that may never actually arrive

author: Persian Proverb (unique, not in prior sets)
persian: کبوتر با کبوتر، باز با باز / کند هم‌جنس با هم‌جنس پرواز
english_translation: Dove with dove, hawk with hawk / Like flies with like through the air.
theme: The natural law that like seeks like — people of similar nature are inevitably drawn together

author: Persian Proverb (unique, not in prior sets)
persian: کار امروز را به فردا میفکن
english_translation: Do not cast today's work to tomorrow.
theme: The fundamental discipline of addressing the present task rather than deferring it to tomorrow

author: Persian Proverb (unique, not in prior sets)
persian: درد بی‌درمان نیست جز مرگ
english_translation: There is no incurable pain except death.
theme: The radical hopefulness that declares all pain curable — only death itself has no remedy

author: Persian Proverb (unique, not in prior sets)
persian: نه هر که چهره برافروخت دلبری داند
english_translation: Not everyone who brightens their face knows how to win hearts.
theme: Outward attractiveness without inner substance unable to captivate a discerning heart

author: Persian Proverb (unique, not in prior sets)
persian: گربه را دُم بریده به خانه می‌آید
english_translation: The cat comes home with its tail cut off.
theme: One who has done wrong inevitably returns bearing the visible marks of the consequences

author: Persian Proverb (unique, not in prior sets)
persian: چراغی که به خانه رواست، به مسجد حرام است
english_translation: The lamp that is right for the home is forbidden in the mosque.
theme: The importance of context in determining the appropriateness of any action or thing

author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi (new, additional quote not in Part 3)
persian: سؤال پرسیدن نصف علم است
english_translation: Asking a question is half of knowledge.
theme: The act of asking the right question as itself constituting half the journey toward knowledge

author: Mulla Sadra (new, additional quote not in Part 3)
persian: شادی حقیقی از معرفت است نه از لذت
english_translation: True joy comes from knowledge, not from pleasure.
theme: Distinguishing the shallow happiness of pleasure from the deep joy of genuine understanding

author: Suhrawardi (new, additional quote not in Part 3)
persian: اشراق دیدنی است نه گفتنی
english_translation: Illumination is to be seen, not to be spoken.
theme: Mystical illumination as a direct experience that fundamentally transcends verbal expression

author: Shams-i-Tabrizi (new, additional quote not in Part 3)
persian: آن که می‌گوید می‌دانم، کم‌تر می‌داند / آن که می‌گوید نمی‌دانم، بیشتر می‌داند
english_translation: One who says 'I know' knows less / One who says 'I do not know' knows more.
theme: The deepest paradox of knowledge: certainty signals shallowness while uncertainty signals depth

author: Simin Behbahani (new, additional quote not in Part 3)
persian: از خاک برمی‌خیزم، چون گل / و با باد می‌روم، چون ابر
english_translation: I rise from the earth like a flower / And go with the wind, like a cloud.
theme: The human life as flowering from the earth and drifting with the wind — beautiful and impermanent

author: Ayn al-Qudat Hamadani (new, additional quote not in Part 3)
persian: کسی که حقیقت را دید، از هر دو دنیا گذشت
english_translation: Whoever has seen the truth has passed beyond both worlds.
theme: True perception of reality as a state that transcends both the present and the future world

author: Bidel Dehlavi (new, additional quote not in Part 3)
persian: جهان آیینه‌ای است که در آن خود را می‌بینی / اگر دیدی که چه هستی، دیدی که جهان چیست
english_translation: The world is a mirror in which you see yourself / If you see what you are, you see what the world is.
theme: The world as the mirror of the self — knowing oneself is knowing the nature of all existence

author: Sa'ib Tabrizi (new, additional quote not in prior sets)
persian: دشمن دانا به از دوست نادان / که دوست نادان خانه‌ات را ویران کند
english_translation: A wise enemy is better than an ignorant friend / For the ignorant friend can ruin your house.
theme: The danger of well-meaning ignorance surpassing the danger of conscious enmity

author: Fighani Shirazi (new, additional quote not in prior sets)
persian: گر صبر کنی، ز غوره انگور شود / وز انگور می ناب، ز می هوش ربود
english_translation: If you are patient, the unripe grape becomes a grape / From the grape comes pure wine, and from wine comes transported awareness.
theme: The chain of patient transformation from raw beginnings to the highest states of awareness

author: Hatif Isfahani (new, additional quote not in Part 3)
persian: گر مؤمن و گر کافر، عاشق همه را / در کوی محبت راه است و مقام
english_translation: Whether believer or unbeliever, love embraces all / In the lane of devotion there is a path and a station for each.
theme: Love's lane as open to all human beings regardless of faith or creed

author: Kalim Kashani (new, additional quote not in prior sets)
persian: وقت گذشته باز نمی‌گردد / پس امروز را دریاب که فردا نیست
english_translation: Time that has passed does not return / So seize today for there may be no tomorrow.
theme: The irreversibility of time as the most powerful argument for seizing the present moment

author: Nima Yushij (new, additional quote not in Part 3)
persian: من می‌نویسم پس هستم / که قلم تنها گواه وجود من است
english_translation: I write, therefore I am / For the pen is the only witness to my existence.
theme: The act of writing as the fundamental act of self-affirmation and proof of one's existence

author: Mehdi Akhavan-Sales (new, additional quote not in Part 3)
persian: ما سرزمین عجیبی داریم / که درد آن شیرین‌تر از شادی‌های دیگران است
english_translation: We have a strange homeland / Whose pain is sweeter than other people's joys.
theme: The paradoxical sweetness of suffering for one's homeland that surpasses foreign joy

author: Forughi Bastami (Abbas Forughi Bastami)
persian: عشق اول قدم است و آخرین / که از اول تا به آخر عشق باید رفت
english_translation: Love is the first step and the last / For from beginning to end, one must travel with love.
theme: Love as both the beginning and the end of the journey — the alpha and omega of all seeking

author: Forughi Bastami (Abbas Forughi Bastami)
persian: دل بی‌عشق ویران است / عشق است که خانه‌ی دل را آباد می‌کند
english_translation: A heart without love is a ruin / It is love that causes the house of the heart to flourish.
theme: Love as the only force capable of transforming the heart from ruin to flourishing dwelling

author: Yahya ibn Muadh al-Razi (new, additional quote not in Part 3)
persian: امید به خدا بیشتر از ترس از خدا ثمر می‌دهد
english_translation: Hope in God bears more fruit than fear of God.
theme: Divine hope as a more generative and creative spiritual force than divine fear

author: Hakim Sanai (new, additional quote not in Part 3)
persian: علم ظاهر است و علم باطن / ظاهر برای تن و باطن برای جان
english_translation: There is outward knowledge and inward knowledge / The outward is for the body and the inward for the soul.
theme: The necessary distinction between external knowledge serving the body and inner knowledge feeding the soul

author: Qabus ibn Wushmagir (new, additional quote not in prior sets)
persian: هر که راز خود به دشمن گفت / دشمن را سلاح داد
english_translation: Whoever reveals their secret to an enemy / Has given the enemy a weapon.
theme: Careless disclosure of one's vulnerabilities as the act of arming one's own enemy

author: Nasir al-Din Tusi (new, additional quote not in prior sets)
persian: معاشرت با نیکان نیکی را آموزد / معاشرت با بدان بدی را تعلیم دهد
english_translation: Association with the good teaches goodness / Association with the bad teaches evil.
theme: The moral environment of one's companions as the most reliable teacher of character

author: Shah Ni'matullah Wali (new, additional quote not in prior sets)
persian: در هر قدم که برمی‌داری، جهانی تازه پیش روست
english_translation: With every step you take, a new world lies ahead.
theme: Each step forward revealing a entirely new world of possibility previously invisible

author: Mir Damad (new, additional quote not in Part 3)
persian: حکیم آن است که از ظاهر به باطن و از باطن به حق برسد
english_translation: The philosopher is one who travels from the outward to the inward, and from the inward to the divine.
theme: The philosopher's path as a threefold journey from surface appearances to inner truth to the divine
